deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous page and this one, Gauss studies the function y = (φ − sin φ)/((4/3) sin³(φ/2)). With x = sin(φ/4), the previous page gives y = 1 + (6/5)x² + (6·8)/(5·7)x⁴ + …. This is the hypergeometric series F(3,1;5/2;x²). It is the sector/triangle function behind the orbit-determination work that appeared in Theoria Motus, 1809. The page has five clusters.

(A) Differential equation for y (top left).
- y = Σ c_k x^{2k}, with c_k/c_{k-1} = (2k+4)/(2k+3), satisfies (x − x³) y' + (3 − 6x²) y = 3.
- The first line ('∂y x³ − ½∂y x⁶ = 3xx∂…') is a garbled false start.
- Substituting x = sin(φ/4):
  - x − x³ = sin(φ/4) cos²(φ/4) = sin²(φ/2)/(4x);
  - 3 − 6x² = 3 cos(φ/2).
  - Result: (sin²(φ/2)/(4x)) dy/dx + 3y cos(φ/2) = 3.
  - [Mine:] since dx = ¼cos(φ/4) dφ, this is equivalent to (2/3) sin(φ/2) dy/dφ + y cos(φ/2) = 1.

(B) Trigonometric identity, with γ = cos(φ/2) and δ = sin(φ/2).
- Since sin³(φ/2) = 8 sin³(φ/4) cos³(φ/4):
  sin²(φ/4)(φ − sin φ)/sin³(φ/2) + 1 = (φ − sin φ)/(8 sin(φ/4) cos³(φ/4)) + 1.
- Rewritten as ½(1−γ)(φ − 2δγ)/δ³ + 1 = ½(1−γ)φ/δ³ + (1−γ)/δ².
  - This uses 1 − γ(1−γ)/δ² = (1−γ)/δ², i.e. δ² + γ² = 1.
- Final form: (½φ + δ)(1−γ)/δ³.
- The next page continues this.

(C) General hypergeometric case and its quadrature.
- Let y = 1 + (m/n)x + m(m+1)/(n(n+1))x² + … = F(m,1;n;x).
- It satisfies (x − x²) y' + (n − 1 − m x) y = n − 1.
- Case (A) is m = 3, n = 5/2 in the variable x².
- Side notes:
  - y = e^u for a general linear ODE y'' + Py' + … = X;
  - the standard integrating factor for y' + Py + Q = 0: y e^{∫P} + ∫Q e^{∫P} dx = C, i.e. with R = e^{∫P}, Ry + ∫QR dx = 0.
- Applied here:
  - P = (n−1−mx)/(x(1−x)) = (n−1)/x − (m−n+1)/(1−x), so R = x^{n−1}(1−x)^{m−n+1};
  - with z = y x^{n−1}(1−x)^{m−n+1}: dz/z = dy/y + P dx = (n−1)dx/(y x(1−x));
  - hence dz = (n−1) x^{n−2}(1−x)^{m−n} dx.
- [Mine:] So F(m,1;n;x) = (n−1) x^{1−n}(1−x)^{n−m−1} ∫₀ˣ t^{n−2}(1−t)^{m−n} dt, the Euler/incomplete-beta integral.

(D) Same function in θ = tan(φ/2) (top right).
- Gauss again writes φ − sin φ = (32/3)x³(1−x²)^{3/2} y and differentiates to get a first-order ODE in φ.
- Then 2 arctan θ − 2θ/(1+θ²), i.e. φ − sin φ with sin φ = 2θ/(1+θ²), equals (4/3)θ³ − (8/5)θ⁵ + (12/7)θ⁷ − ….
- Hence φ − sin φ = (4/3)θ³(1 − (6/5)θ² + (9/7)θ⁴ − (12/9)θ⁶ + (15/11)θ⁸ − …), general coefficient 3k/(2k+1).
- Two products are formed:
  - with (1+θ²)^{3/2} = 1 + (3/2)θ² + (3/8)θ⁴: gives y = 1 + (3/10)θ² − (39/280)θ⁴ (the partial sums 105, 360, 504 are visible);
  - with (1+θ²)³: gives 1 + (9/5)θ² + (24/35)θ⁴ − (8/105)θ⁶.
- Gauss then begins converting S0 = 1 − (6/5)t + (9/7)t² − (12/9)t³ + (15/11)t⁴ into a continued fraction by repeated subtraction and division:
  - S0 = 1 − (6/5)t S1, with S1 = 1 − (15/14)t + (10/9)t² − (25/22)t³;
  - S1 = S0 + (9/70)t S2, with S2 = 1 − (110/81)t + (455/297)t².
- This is the algorithm written out on the next page: P = Q − αR, Q = R − βS, ….

(E) Two continued fractions by the same scheme (bottom right).
- (E1) Lambert's continued fraction for tan:
  - P0 = cos x, P1 = sin x/x, P2 = 1 − x²/10 + x⁴/280 − x⁶/15120, P3 = 1 − x²/14 + x⁴/504, P4 = 1 − x²/18;
  - recursion P_{k} = P_{k+1} − x²/(4(k+1)²−1) · P_{k+2}, with multipliers 1/3, 1/15, 1/35, 1/63;
  - hence tan φ = φ/(1 − (1/3)φ²/(1 − (1/15)φ²/…)).
- (E2) Continued fraction for 3(x − sin x)/(x(1 − cos x)) = Q1/Q0:
  - Q0 = 2(1−cos x)/x² = 1 − x²/(3·4) + x⁴/(3·4·5·6) − …;
  - Q1 = 6(x − sin x)/x³ = 1 − x²/(4·5) + x⁴/(4·5·6·7) − …;
  - Q0 = Q1 − (1/30)x²Q2, with Q2 = 1 − x²/21 + x⁴/1008 − x⁶/83160;
  - Q1 = Q2 − (1/420)x²Q3, with Q3 = 1 − x²/12 + x⁴/528 − 7x⁶/308880;
  - Q2 = Q3 + (1/28)x²Q4, with Q4 = 1 − (5/198)x² + 23x⁴/(45·6·22·13);
  - next multiplier Q3 − Q4 = −(23/396)x²…; the row '1 − 4…' is unfinished.
  - Hence 3(x − sin x)/(x(1 − cos x)) = 1/(1 − (x²/30)/(1 − (x²/420)/(1 + (x²/28)/(1 − (23x²/396)/…)))).

All of this serves the computation of φ − sin φ (elliptic sector minus triangle) for orbit determination. It leads to the continued fractions of Theoria Motus art. 90 and to the 1812 hypergeometric continued fraction.
errors: The φ-form of the ODE is off by a factor 2. Gauss writes ∂φ(1−cosφ) = (4/3)sin³(½φ)∂y + 4y sin²(½φ)cos(½φ)∂φ and then 1 = (2/3)sin(½φ) dy/dφ + 2y cos(½φ). The derivative of (4/3)sin³(½φ) is 2 sin²(½φ)cos(½φ), so the correct result is 1 = (2/3)sin(½φ) dy/dφ + y cos(½φ). This also agrees with his own x-form, (sin²(½φ)/(4x)) y' + 3y cos(½φ) = 3.

In the z-computation the coefficient of dx/(1−x) must be (m−n+1), consistent with his own z = y x^{n−1}(1−x)^{m−n+1}. The transcription's '(m+n+1)' is either a slip or a misreading. The final results dz/z = (n−1)dx/(yx(1−x)) and dz = (n−1)x^{n−2}(1−x)^{m−n}dx are correct.
In the (x − sin x)/(1 − cos x) continued fraction, the third multiplier should be +1/28 (= −1/21 + 1/12); the transcription reads +1/18.
The fourth multiplier should be −23/396 (= −1/12 + 5/198), but −7/132 (= −21/396) is written. This is probably a Gauss slip, since the 23 reappears correctly in his Q4 coefficient.
The first row of the tan scheme, cos x, needs −1/720 as its x⁶ coefficient; it reads −1/120. Either a slip or a misreading; the later rows (1/15120 etc.) are computed correctly.
The opening line '∂y x³ − ½∂y x⁶ = 3xx∂' is an abandoned or garbled start. The 'x^m∂x^{n−1}y / −x^n∂x^m y' line is also not fully interpretable.

deep.surprise_reason: This is working material for the Theoria Motus sector–triangle continued fractions and a precursor of the 1812 hypergeometric work, both known to be Gauss's. Seeing the hypergeometric ODE, its Euler-integral solution and a series-to-continued-fraction scheme in 1805 is a nice dated detail but not a new result. The (x−sinx)/(1−cosx) continued fraction is an ad hoc computation, not a recognised theorem.

transcription_corrections: In dz/z the coefficient of dx/(1−x) should read (m−n+1), not (m+n+1), consistent with z = y x^{n−1}(1−x)^{m−n+1}.
'(n−1)(1−x) + (m+n−1)x' is the numerator of the partial-fraction combination; it should involve (m−n+1)x, giving n−1−mx.
The equation transcribed as 'φ sinφ/(1−cosφ) = φ²/(1−⅓φφ/(1−1/15φφ))' is Lambert's 'tang φ = sinφ/cosφ = φ/(1 − ⅓φφ/(1 − 1/15 φφ …))'; compare the next page.
In the (x−sinx)/(1−cosx) block, first row '1 − 1/(2.4)' should be '1 − 1/(3.4)', i.e. 2(1−cos x)/x².
'23/(4.5.6.22.13)' should be read '23/(45.6.22.13)' = 23/77220, which is the correct value.
'−1/(4.5.6 99.26)' has numerator 7: the correct value is −7/308880.
